entries.gap: repair_timing -hold makes one pass for each violating end point and then stops, also when violations remain. It also stops at the maximum buffer count (-max_buffer_percent of the instance count; error RSZ-0060). The warning RSZ-0064 ('unable to repair all hold checks within margin') does not tell which of these happened, and it is also given when all checks are met but not the margin.
entries.symptom: A block with many short flop-to-flop paths ends the hold repair with RSZ-0064 and negative hold slack, or with RSZ-0060. The number of buffers in the last row of the progress table is equal to the number of violating end points, or to the buffer limit.
entries.workaround: Read the progress table before you name a cause (openroad adapter, operation parse). At the buffer limit: raise the limit (LibreLane: PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT, at most 100). After one sweep: run the repair again on its own output (librelane adapter, operation replay with state_in of the first replay), or reduce the violating end points before the repair.
entries.evidence: examples/shreg-sg13g2 with IHP SG13G2: 11976 end points, 11976 buffers, worst slack -0.40 ns after one sweep; a second sweep ends with no negative slack (evals flow-repair-progress, flow-step-replay)

entries.gap: The Verilog reader of OpenSTA does not accept the keyword 'signed' in a port or wire declaration of a gate-level netlist.
entries.symptom: read_verilog stops with 'syntax error' at the line of the declaration. A script that does not check the exit code of the timing run then reports old result files.
entries.workaround: Remove the keyword from the netlist that the timing tool reads (it has no effect on a gate-level netlist), for example with sed after write_verilog. Check that the report files are newer than the netlist.
entries.evidence: a signed FIR filter synthesized with Yosys 0.67 (write_verilog -noattr) for IHP SG13G2: OpenSTA 2.7.0 and 3.1.0 stop at the port declaration (eval flow-no-work)
